full_judgment:
2. The opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted the above suit for permanent injunction impleading the petitioners and others as defendants and praying for restraining the defendant No. 1 Uma Rani Roy from selling the suit land measuring 41 decimal stating, inter alia, that defendant No. 1 Uma Rani Roy got the suit land by virtue of a will of her father-in-law and also by amicable partition with her son Kashab Chandra Roy; that by a registered kabala dated 18.8.69 defendant No. 1 Uma Rani Roy transferred the land in suit to the plaintiffs and since then the plaintiffs are in possession by growing crops, that as the boundary of the land was not correctly given in the said kabala the plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 149 of 1972 against defendant No. 1 Uma Rani Roy for rectification of the said kabala and the same was decreed ex pane; that at the instance of the plaintiffs a criminal case under section 145 CrPC was started and the land was attached. The Officer-in-charge, Lakhai, was appointed receiver thereof who used to grow paddy through defendant No. 5 and the said receiver was depositing the sale proceeds of paddy grown on the suit land in a local bank. 

 4. The defendants No. 2 to 4 contested the prayer of the plaintiffs for temporary injunction by filing written objection contending, inter alia, that defendant No. 1 Uma Rani Roy entered into a contract for sale of the land to defendant No. 2 on 15th Mag, 1375 BS by executing a bainapatra and thereafter she executed and registered a sale deed in favour of the defendants on 22.6.72 for valuable consideration and since then they are in possession; the alleged ex pane decree passed in Title Suit No. 149 of 1972 against defendant No. 1 Uma Rani Roy is not binding upon defendants No. 2 to 4 inasmuch as the land had already been transferred to them (defendants No. 2 to 4) by defendant No. 1 long before the said ex pane decree in Title Suit No. 149 of 1972.
